warrant:
default.ini is an official upstream example deck (the stock LambdaCDM default deck (Planck-like fiducial parameters, halofit off)); the module's own excluded note records that the four upstream .ini decks are not vendored under code/class/ at this pin, so this check ships a byte-identical copy under ic/, the same pattern explanatory-end-to-end and thermodynamics already use for their own deck inputs. Every physical output file the deck writes is graded: the unlensed and lensed CMB spectra (all seven physical columns: TT, EE, TE, BB, phiphi, Tphi, Ephi) at an exact integer multipole key, and the matter power spectrum (and, where halofit runs, the baryon+CDM-only and non-linear variants) at a wavenumber key, all at atol=0, rtol=1e-6, tracking the driver's own high-precision print format. A wrong transfer projection, harmonic normalization, lensing convolution or non-linear correction anywhere in the pipeline will move at least one graded column beyond its bound on this independent, differently-parameterized cosmology from the C-driver test decks. The live omega_cdm variant (1e-9 relative, an active input this deck controls) moves every graded output file, unlike the identical variants the other checks in this leaf use because their upstream test drivers fix every input internally. The same-input -O2 build supplies the numerical-floor evidence.

Revised after the class-rev728-final3 calibration run: CLASS's perturbation and Fourier k/tau sampling is adaptive (perturbations.c:1887-1951 accumulates conformal time in a floating-point loop terminated by a floating-point comparison); measured on the x86 worker's live omega_cdm (1e-9 relative) variant, this discretizes the auto-spectra (TT, EE, PP, and the matter power spectrum) at the few-times-1e-4-relative level and moves the cross-spectra (TE, TP, EP) -- which legitimately cross zero -- by amounts that blow up under a pure relative bound near their zero-crossings. rtol=1e-3 tracks the measured auto-spectra floor with room to spare (measured worst 3.9e-4 TT, 1.6e-3 EE, 8.1e-4 PP across the three deck checks); the small per-column atol on ee/te/tp/ep absorbs the zero-crossing floor (measured worst needed atol 6.97e-16/9.61e-15/2.35e-16/4.25e-17 respectively across the three deck checks, each with roughly 10-20x margin here) without loosening the bound anywhere the reference is not near zero.
